referents.why: Third masculine singular suffix on 'say to him' in a command about standing before Pharaoh; Pharaoh (w13) is the only agreeing person in the verse and the one Moses is sent to.
referents.category: pronoun resolved to the person a command is directed at

referents.why: First person 'my' in 'my people' sits inside the quoted message introduced by 'thus says Yahweh' (cl6); the speaker of that speech is the LORD (w25).
referents.category: first person inside a quoted message

referents.why: First person suffix 'serve me' is inside the same quoted message, whose speaker is the LORD (w25).
referents.category: first person inside a quoted message

referents.why: Implied 'you' of an imperative in the LORD's speech to Moses (cl0); second masculine singular agrees with Moses.
referents.category: implied subject of a command in the outer speech

referents.why: Implied 'you' of the imperative 'present yourself', joined by waw to the preceding command, in the LORD's speech to Moses.
referents.category: implied subject of a command in the outer speech

referents.why: Implied 'you' of the weqatal 'you will say to him', continuing the instructions the LORD gives Moses; it introduces the inner message but belongs to the outer speech.
referents.category: clause that introduces a speech belongs to the speech around it

referents.why: Implied 'you' of 'let go my people' is inside the message Moses is to deliver, so it is the addressee of that message: Pharaoh, the one he is told to say it to (cl5, 'to him').
referents.category: implied subject of a command in a commanded speech

referents.why: Third masculine plural 'they may serve me' refers to the people just named as the object of the release (w27, 'my people'); 'people' is a collective that takes a plural verb.
referents.category: collective noun taken by a plural verb

links.why: cl3 is the presentative 'there!' inside the speech, not a narrative event; the narrative 'then' belongs to the wayyiqtol cl0 and does not run from a clause inside the quoted speech back to it.
links.category: narrative then wrongly applied to a clause inside a speech

links.why: Separate-word waw joining two commands at one level (rise early, and present yourself).
The weqatal 'you will say' continues what precedes it; Pharaoh's going out is the occasion at which Moses is to speak. The scope of the time clause over cl2 as well is left in cant_tell.
Waw + yiqtol in a different person (you let go, they may serve) after a command is 'so that', not a plain 'and'; it is replaced by a purpose link.
links.category: plain and read where the person changes after a command

links.why: Command, then waw + yiqtol in a different person (second to third): what the release is for - that they may worship.
links.category: purpose after a command with change of person

links.why: The saying clause 'the LORD said to Moses' is followed by a run of commands joined by 'and' at one level; the content is that whole imperative group.
links.category: speech and its collection of commands

links.why: 'You will say to him' introduces what Moses is to say, which is the quoted message framed by 'thus says Yahweh'; the commanded turn is the content.
links.category: nested speech commanded to be said

links.why: 'Thus says Yahweh' is a saying frame and what follows (let my people go, that they may serve me) is the message; the said clause is the imperative group, embedded in the saying.

groups.why: The LORD speaks to Moses (cl0). The commands become one imperative group and the commanded message is the nested turn1 as a part, as nesting is to be recorded; cl3 and cl4 are the time setting inside the speech.
groups.category: speech holding a command group and a nested commanded speech

groups.why: Rise early, present yourself and say are commands joined by 'and' at one level, so one group with several command members; the builder had cl2 as a mere part, and the weqatal cl5 continues the chain as a further instruction.
groups.category: commands joined by and at one level are one imperative group

groups.why: The message introduced by 'thus says Yahweh' is the LORD's, to be delivered to Pharaoh (cl5, 'to him'); the builder gave no addressee and listed cl7 and cl8 separately instead of the imperative group.
groups.category: nested speech with sender and addressee supplied

groups.why: 'Let my people go' with waw + yiqtol in a different person is a purpose, so cl8 is the aim, not a plain part; it is not an effect, which is the role for waw + third-person weqatal after a command.
groups.category: aim of a command after change of person

none_fit.what: The presentative 'there!' with a participle clause ('he is going out to the water') sets the time or occasion of the standing and the saying (when Pharaoh goes out); no link type expresses a time setting by a presentative plus participle, and no group role holds it other than a bare part of the speech.
The participle cl4 ('going out') has an implied subject (Pharaoh, w13) that the slot list does not carry; there is no slot id against which to record the choice.

cant_tell.what: Whether the time clause cl3/cl4 governs the standing before Pharaoh (cl2), only the saying (cl5), or both
cant_tell.why: One presentative and no connective; the form does not say which command it sets the time for. It reads naturally as the occasion for the meeting and the message together.

cant_tell.what: Whether the weqatal cl5 is a further command in the chain or a result of the time clause
cant_tell.why: A weqatal after imperatives is usually a sequential instruction, but it is grammatically also the continuation of the participle clause cl4; both readings are kept (the then link and membership in the command group).
